summary: The study investigates the mechanical properties of HfO2 and Al2O3 thin films deposited by Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) on p-type Si wafers. The films were characterized using nanoindentation and continuous stiffness measurement (CSM) techniques to determine their hardness and modulus. The results show that both materials have similar mechanical properties, with HfO2 forming a hafnium silicate interlayer at the Si interface, which affects its nanoindentation properties.
evidence: The text states: 'HfO2 and Al2O3 have been fabricated using atomic layer deposition on 100 p-type Si wafers. Using nanoindentation and the continuous stiffness method, we report the elastomechanical properties of HfO2 and Al2O3 on Si. ALD HfO2 thin films were measured to have a hardness of 9.5 GPa and a modulus of 220–40 GPa, whereas the ALD Al2O3 thin films have a hardness of 10.5 GPa and a modulus of 220–40 GPa. The two materials are also distinguished by very different interface properties. HfO2 forms a hafnium silicate interlayer, which influences its nanoindentation properties close to the interface with the Si substrate, while Al2O3 does not exhibit any interlayer.'
